definitions.explanation: An action carried out suddenly and without advance warning, typically an inspection, test, or check. Almost always used as a modifier with の or in compound form.

examples.japanese: {抜|ぬ}き{打|う}ちテストがあった。
{抜|ぬ}き{打|う}ちで{検査|けんさ}が{行|おこな}われた。
examples.english: An unannounced inspection was carried out.

examples.japanese: {保健所|ほけんじょ}が{抜|ぬ}き{打|う}ちで{飲食店|いんしょくてん}を{調|しら}べることがある。
examples.english: The health center sometimes inspects restaurants without prior notice.

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}は{抜|ぬ}き{打|う}ちの{小|しょう}テストが{好|す}きだ。
examples.english: The teacher likes giving pop quizzes.

notes:
Originally a kendo term meaning to draw and strike in one motion, {抜|ぬ}き{打|う}ち now primarily refers to doing something without advance notice. It is almost always used as a noun modifier: {抜|ぬ}き{打|う}ちの〜 or {抜|ぬ}き{打|う}ちで.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {抜|ぬ}き{打|う}ちテスト: surprise test; pop quiz
- {抜|ぬ}き{打|う}ち{検査|けんさ}: surprise inspection
- {抜|ぬ}き{打|う}ちで{調|しら}べる: to investigate without notice
- {抜|ぬ}き{打|う}ち{監査|かんさ}: surprise audit

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {突然|とつぜん}: sudden — describes any abrupt event, not specifically planned surprise actions
- {不意|ふい}に: unexpectedly — focuses on the recipient's lack of awareness
- {予告|よこく}なし: without advance notice — more neutral and explanatory
